resources.string: Hold a button to pick the time. Tap an entry to change its time.

Coffee • One cup = 2 tsp instant ≈ 110 mg caffeine. This is an estimate: one teaspoon holds roughly 30–90 mg depending on brand and how heaped it is. Change it in settings if your coffee is stronger or weaker. • Up to 400 mg a day is the amount the US FDA says is generally not linked to harm in healthy adults. Pregnancy, heart problems or medication can change that. • No research gives a minimum gap between cups. EFSA says single doses up to 200 mg are fine, so the app spreads your remaining cups evenly up to the evening cutoff instead. • Last coffee 9 h before bed. A 2023 meta-analysis found a cup of coffee (~107 mg) should be drunk at least 8.8 h before bedtime to avoid cutting sleep short. Caffeine half-life is about 5 h on average but ranges from 2 to 10 h between people.
Food • Last food 3 h before bed. Gastroenterology guidelines (ACG 2022) advise not eating 2–3 h before lying down; dinner less than 3 h before bed is linked to more reflux. • Breaks between meals (3 h) and after a snack (2 h) are a common rule of thumb, not a medical rule. A normal meal leaves the stomach in about 3–4 h. Adjust them in settings.
Sources FDA, Spilling the beans: https://www.fda.gov/consumers/consumer-updates/spilling-beans-how-much-caffeine-too-much EFSA, caffeine: https://www.efsa.europa.eu/en/topics/topic/caffeine Gardiner et al. 2023, Sleep Medicine Reviews: https://eprints.leedsbeckett.ac.uk/id/eprint/9625/ ACG GERD guideline 2022: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8754510/
